neighbours.label: the negator after can/could in ability idioms: the 't of can't/couldn't, or never/hardly after could (couldn't resist, can't believe, could hardly hear)
fire: She laughed so hard she couldn't breathe for a moment.
Honestly, I can't thank you enough for all your help.
The puppy was so cute that we couldn't resist taking him home.
As a kid, my brother could never sit still in church.
Over all that noise we could hardly hear the speaker.
He couldn't take his eyes off the sports car in the window.
Looking back, I can't believe how fast this year has gone by.
When I saw his face, I couldn't help but laugh.
quiet: She laughed so hard she started to cry for a moment.
Honestly, I want to thank you for all your help.
The puppy was so cute that we decided to take him home.
As a kid, my brother didn't like sitting in church.
Over all that noise we heard the speaker quite clearly.
He kept staring at the sports car in the window.
Looking back, I am amazed at how fast this year has gone by.
When I saw his face, I started to laugh.

notes: Probe: couldn't 0.40, could never 0.52, could hardly 0.49, can't 0.20; didn't/isn't/won't 0.07-0.09, does not 0.005. So not general negation.
